subject: Chronicle: snapshot retirement & subprocessor takedown plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@healixhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Chronicle: snapshot retirement & subprocessor takedown plan

Hi Samir —

Quick note to surface our proposed timeline for retiring older immutable snapshots tied to your account (internal name: "chronicle"). We ran the inventory and attached a manifest that maps snapshots to subprocessor storage buckets. High level:

- Scope: snapshots created before 2025-01-01, stored in three S3 buckets across two subprocessors.
- Proposed schedule: staged retirement starting 2026-11-01; final purge window 2027-03-01.
- Recovery/rollback: we expect a 30-day canary window before any irreversible deletes; we will retain a temporary chained copy for 60 days after canary.

Ask: can Healix confirm if there are any active legal holds, ongoing investigations, or regulatory audits that require longer retention? If so we will pause and produce a tailored hold schedule. Also please confirm whether the listed subprocessors (attached) are acceptable for the takedown notices we’ll issue; we will need contact points to complete notices.

Attachments: chronicle_retire_manifest.csv (map of snapshots -> subprocessor), subprocessor_inventory_v2.pdf (current contracts + endpoints).

I’m looping in Kim and Priyom for the operational and DPA side. If you’d prefer a 30-minute sync this week to walk the manifest, happy to schedule.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@healixhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@healixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chronicle: snapshot retirement & subprocessor takedown plan

Sergio, thanks for the summary and the manifest. A couple quick clarifications before we confirm: 

1) Recovery window: when you say "chained copy for 60 days after canary," does that imply we will still be able to restore full datasets for that period, or will restorations require Redwood support?
2) Immutable backup question: are any of the subprocessor buckets write-once/immutable (WORM) configured such that deletion requires a longer process?
3) Audit/holds: Legal Ops are checking, but we have a pending HIE audit that could request historical logs back to 2024.

If possible, can you flag which snapshots would be considered high-risk (PHI-proximal) vs. lower-risk for a staggered approach? We prefer to avoid a blanket pause if only a small subset is flagged.

–Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Platform Ops
Healix Health
samir.patel@healixhealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@healixhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chronicle: snapshot retirement & subprocessor takedown plan

Hi Samir,

Thanks — I pulled the manifest and annotated risk levels. Short answers to your questions: 

1) Restoration: during the 60-day chained-copy period we maintain a mountable copy. Restores can be initiated by Healix self-serve for single-file/object restores via the Console; for full dataset restorations we recommend Redwood run the restore to avoid partial-index issues. We will document the exact restore runbook and provide a ticket template.

2) WORM / immutability: one subprocessor (WestCloud Storage) enforces object lock on a per-bucket basis. For those buckets we cannot perform a fast delete; there is a 7-day retention overlay and a formal release process that WestCloud requires (they need signed deletion orders). We flagged those snapshot IDs in the manifest and added WestCloud contact points.

3) Audit/holds: if Legal Ops needs data back to 2024 then we should treat those snapshot IDs as "hold" and exclude them from the November canary.

Recommendation / proposed change to schedule (to reduce blast radius):
- Phase 0 (now–2026-10-15): finalize hold list from Healix legal; Redwood to produce an evidence bundle for flagged snapshots.
- Phase 1 - Canary (2026-11-01 to 2026-12-01): select 5% of non-held, non-WORM snapshots (low-risk) for canary retire. Monitor restore success metrics and cost delta.
- Phase 2 - Staged purge (2026-12-15 to 2027-03-01): progressively retire remaining eligible snapshots in cohorts by risk tier (low -> medium -> high), with WestCloud-run deletions scheduled separately per their SLA.

I attached a short runbook excerpt for canary restores and the subprocessor contact list. If this works for you we will convert Phase 1 into a change request and schedule the notices.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Principal Systems Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_v2.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@healixhealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Legal Ops <legalops@healixhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chronicle: snapshot retirement & subprocessor takedown plan

Samir, thanks for the quick turn. Per Kim's notes, Redwood will: 

- Hold any snapshot IDs formally flagged by Healix legal (please send list by 2026-10-15).
- Proceed with Phase 1 canary on 2026-11-01 limited to low-risk items; Redwood will provide a pre-canary evidence package and a DocuSign deletion authorization for WestCloud where required.
- Coordinate DPA amendment language for subprocessor takedown (minor addendum to cover targeted decommission and deletion orders). I will pull in Procurement to issue an amendment and share a draft by 2026-10-01.

Action items:
- Healix Legal: deliver hold list (IDs + reason) by 2026-10-15.
- Healix Ops (Samir): confirm contact for WestCloud deletions and whether you want Redwood to act as authorized agent for releases.
- Redwood (Priyom): draft DPA addendum and upload DocuSign link; schedule pre-canary sync for 2026-10-20.

If any audits/holds come in after the 10/15 cut-off we will treat them as emergency holds and pause deletion activity until legal sign-off.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Manager, Compliance & Risk Operations
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.inference.com
